identity: Independent Jai implementations derived from public declarations/layouts. An initial overly broad declaration search incidentally displayed some reference local declarations; they were not reused. No reference implementation bodies copied.
primary_contract: Maintained OpenJai public Basic declarations in corpus/upstream/withlang-dev--open-jai/modules/Basic/module.jai; legacy APIs additive where compatible.

limits: Classification is ASCII; is_alnum includes underscore.
Integer parser supports base 2 through 36 and integer widths up to 64 bits; overflow fails without consuming input.
Float parser recognizes decimal fractions and decimal exponents, not hexadecimal/locale/NaN/Inf forms; correctly rounded conversion not established.
Pointer advance uses newer value/count parameter names with a compatible count=1 convenience default; original amount= named argument is not retained.
Float aliases are callable wrappers because frozen parser rejects #bake_constants.
Primitive conversions are intended for integers up to 64 bits; float conversions are not supported.

Arithmetic wraps modulo 2^128 through bounded explicit carry/borrow helpers, without requiring #no_aoc. Division reports zero divisor and signed minimum/-1 overflow. Shifts at least 128 saturate to zero or signed fill.
Portable shift-add multiplication and restoring division replace CPU assembly; no performance equivalence established.
Apollo_Time uses newer independent struct low:u64/high:s64 rather than legacy isa S128; explicit operators preserve common arithmetic.
Primary to_float64_seconds returns one float64; the legacy checked tuple is exposed as to_float64_seconds_checked. Invalid primary conversion yields zero.
Calendar is undeclared in maintained OpenJai source; to_calendar and calendar_to_string(Calendar) are unavailable. Calendar_Time is an explicitly legacy layout.
Integer rounding is nearest with halves away from zero. Exact upstream rounding/format rendering parity is not established.
Calendar_Time rendering is YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.mmm or ISO with UTC Z; LOCAL has no inferred offset.
OS clock acquisition, timespec conversion, timezone conversion, and calendar validation are external responsibilities.
Float time conversions have float64 precision and are not exact femtosecond round trips.

Newer format factories return temporary strings. Exact legacy factory parameters/defaults and formatter-record returns are available under Legacy_Print; same-name unqualified factories intentionally remain maintained string contracts.
Print_Style retains maintained three-pointer layout; legacy by-value defaults, array formatting default, custom struct callback, indentation state, and log_runtime_errors are not retained.
Adds only print_style to compiler-managed context rather than duplicating newer divergent Context/Type_Info schemas.
Formatting supports lone %, zero-based %N, and %% escapes. Exact undocumented upstream selector semantics are unverified.
Integer bases are 2 through 36 and digit grouping is at most 65535.

Float precision is limited to 18 requested digits. DECIMAL rounds at fractional precision, SCIENTIFIC at fractional significand precision, and maintained SHORTEST uses general notation with significant-digit precision (six by default), rather than round-trip shortest. Independently authored exact integer conversion bodies are syntax-accepted but not behavior-validated.
Float width means left space padding to minimum total bytes; exact legacy width semantics unverified.

Records skip constants/imports and cap recursion at 16; unions fail explicitly because active-member metadata is absent. Named enum values and flags are supported. Procedure type descriptors render parameter/result types and represented calling flags; source names/defaults/variadic details absent from metadata cannot be reconstructed.
Strings are quoted/escaped inside arrays and records. Ordinary pointer values print addresses; explicit formatStruct pointer arguments read their declared struct pointee.
Original buffer_to_string_without_copy(value builder) and append_indentation(context legacy depth) unavailable; no unsafe stack view or fabricated indentation state.
print/log counts represent submitted bytes because Runtime_Support.write_string returns void; OS write failure counts cannot be reported by this API.
Formatting errors append explicit markers and return false/-1 where the public result supports status; sprint/tprint retain rendered diagnostics.

Explicit formatFloatRoundtrip uses adjacent IEEE binary64 rounding intervals to select up to 17 significant digits and a compact fixed/scientific spelling; actual module behavior has not yet executed.

Finite conversion uses a bounded 36-u32-limb integer workspace and 344 output digits; portability assumes IEEE-754 binary64 representation. Exact large DECIMAL expansion can differ from upstream approximate recorded expansions.

float_conversion.maintained_mode_contract: SHORTEST defaults to six significant digits and general fixed/scientific notation, matching the public recorded 1234567.89 -> 1.23457e+06 consumer; explicit formatFloatRoundtrip is an additive extension.
float_conversion.kernel: IEEE-754 mantissa/exponent decomposition; bounded rational radix digit extraction; nearest-even precision rounding; round-trip interval termination uses even-mantissa inclusive midpoint bounds and asymmetric lower spacing at powers of two.
limits: Syntax checking is not behavioral proof.
Public decimal parsing remains approximate and is not used as a round-trip oracle.
Exact huge fixed DECIMAL digits can differ from upstream approximate recorded expansion.
Historical zero-removal whitespace details remain unverified.

revision_notes: Legacy factory signatures/defaults now available under Legacy_Print, preserving maintained same-name factories.
Formatter reflection unwrap uses actual stored #as Formatter member byte offset; direct Formatter boxes are also supported.
Int128 carry/borrow now explicit through bounded 32-bit sums, independent of arithmetic overflow-check policy.
Signed negative zero integer parsing no longer performs an overflowing ~0+1.

Enum flags decompose through declared values with an explicit hexadecimal remainder; procedure type rendering uses actual argument and result descriptors; explicit struct pointers accepted by formatStruct.
Int128 division bit indices cast to bounded u8 counts so signed counters do not mix with u64 operands.
Baked shifts normalize counts with x&63 and (64-shift)&63, preserving the public $$x:u8 signatures while avoiding specialization-time underflow in skipped runtime branches.
Signed left/logical shifts use explicit U128 intermediates so their nominal operator input is retained by the current source binder.
String integer width masks and enum width masks cast bounded bit counts to u8; integer alphabet indexing converts bounded remainders to the signed indexing domain.
Format selector accumulation checks (INT64_MAX-digit)/10 before multiplication, including the final overflowing 8/9 boundary.
Exact bounded integer finite formatting preserves maintained mode signatures and SHORTEST six-significant default; additive formatFloatRoundtrip opts into interval-based round-trip digit generation.
Float special-value handling reads IEEE exponent/fraction bits, preserves signed zero, and avoids floating-to-integer casts of nonfinite values.
Finite DECIMAL remains fixed across binary64 magnitudes rather than falling back to scientific at 1e18; exact precision rounding uses nearest-even.
Negative width values are checked before subtracting rendered byte counts, avoiding signed underflow.

calendar_schema_evidence.decision: No Calendar declaration or stored fields supplied by these contract inputs; current Calendar APIs remain unimplemented rather than inventing a layout. Declared Calendar_Time is explicitly legacy.
